Three snow monkeys sunk to their chins at the far end, the smallest one eyes shut, a wet leaf plastered flat to the top of its head.
A single small macaque sits on the rim, a folded cloth balanced precisely on its head, expression entirely serious about the arrangement.
A small monkey crouched at the lip, coiling to drop in, while the older ones at the far end pay it absolutely no attention.
A young deer standing small on the far rim, nose hovering a finger's width above the water, deeply uncertain about what it is smelling.
A small cat, no bigger than a rim stone, curled on a warm flat stone at the near edge, one paw draped over its own face, profoundly asleep and unavailable.
A small cat sits upright on the eave above, watching the water below with total suspicion and no intention of getting closer.
A crowd of small orange and white carp, tiny at mid-distance, jammed into the cold channel at the side, tails overlapping, every one of them aimed the same wrong direction.
One fat pale carp small at the far edge, nosing at a floating leaf with the calm confidence of a carp expecting to find something better.
A raccoon-dog small at the top of the bank, caught mid-decision, one front paw raised, reconsidering whatever plan it arrived with.
A heron standing tiny and perfectly still on the far rim, one leg raised, committed to the pose for reasons only the heron understands.
Three sparrows lined along a bamboo rail at mid-distance, two facing the water, one facing firmly the other way, unmoved by peer pressure.
A small fox sitting at the very edge of the light, tail curled neatly round its feet, watching without offering any further information.
A hare small on the snow beyond the rim, ears straight up, mid-freeze, absolutely convinced something just moved.
A tiny frog sitting on a floating wooden lid at the near edge, going nowhere, blinking once, satisfied with the lid as a destination.
A small monkey leaning far over the rim, one arm fully extended toward a floating fruit just out of reach, the other arm doing nothing helpful.
A pair of ducks small at the far end, one drifting in a slow circle, the other asleep mid-paddle with its bill tucked completely away.
A squirrel small on a branch above, both cheeks visibly packed to capacity, pausing to look down as if it forgot what it was doing.
A cat small at the step, one paw resting in the water, pulling it back, reconsidering, placing it in again, making no progress.
A small owl, round and compact on a post at the edge of the frame, rotating its head to an angle that solves nothing.
A little group of monkeys at the far rim grooming each other, one at the outside holding a stolen towel it has no plan for.
Two snow monkeys and one very small one sunk chin-deep at the far end, the small one wearing a wet bamboo leaf it did not choose.
A single sparrow, tiny on the far rim, hopping sideways along the stone edge in a direction that leads only back to where it started.
A small tanuki sitting just beyond the rim on the bank, staring at its own reflection with an expression of genuine philosophical concern.
A small monkey sitting at mid-distance on the rim's edge dangling both feet into the water, then immediately pulling one back up.
Three carp small at the far edge nosing the rim in a slow rotation, the largest one bumping the smallest one off its chosen spot repeatedly.
